bull.b: Fold is broadening from bitcoin rewards into deposits, balances and credit, creating more ways to engage customers and monetize activity. Early adoption across several products supports a more diversified platform and could deepen relationships as usage and distribution expand.

The gift card channel is producing meaningful growth in custody and trading revenue while also expanding customer acquisition through TikTok and other distributors. A broader distribution pipeline gives Fold a potentially repeatable route to reach users beyond its core bitcoin audience.

Lower operating costs and reduced interest expense indicate improving expense discipline, while cash and positive working capital provide near-term operating flexibility. These factors can extend the runway for product development as management works toward positive cash flow.

bear.b: The sharp decline in revenue and transaction activity shows that Fold's established business remains under pressure despite newer product launches. Lower volumes can reduce payment-related economics and make it harder for emerging products to offset weakness at sufficient scale.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow limits Fold's ability to fund growth internally and leaves the company dependent on financing or further cost reductions. Deep losses also make sustained investment in products more difficult until revenue growth converts into stronger margins.

bear.t: Credit Card Financing and Risk Uncertainty
bear.b: Expansion of the credit card product depends on obtaining external receivables financing, so growth is constrained while discussions continue. The program also has limited historical loss data, making future credit performance and the appropriate funding structure less certain.
